title: Modular annular photocatalytic membrane reactor for micropollutant degradation
author: Leupold, Reuschenbach, et al.
materials: Prior to the experiments, the UV–Vis spectrum of AMX (50 µM) and the light reflectance spectrum of the TiO2-PES membrane were determined as described in section S3 (SI). As shown in Fig. 4, AMX absorbs light at wavelengths below 300 nm, which overlaps with the emission spectrum of the medium-pressure lamp used in this study. This indicates that direct photolysis of AMX takes place, if no UV cut-off filter is applied. Furthermore, the reflectance spectrum of TiO2-PES reaches its minimum at 350 nm (Fig. 4b), suggesting that incident UV light at this wavelength provides sufficient energy to overcome the band gap of the immobilized TiO2 and generate electron-hole (e-/h+) pairs. Therefore, in applications where the absorption spectrum of AMX overlaps with the emission spectrum of the light source and the excitation wavelength of the photocatalyst, the system can effectively integrate photolytic and photocatalytic processes. However, the explicit contribution of the photocatalyst in such scenarios remains unclear.

steps.title: Assemble reactor and install sensors
steps.instruction: Mount the borosilicate reaction chamber (2.25 L) to the anodized aluminium split flange using a silicone metal‑to‑glass seal; attach the aluminium lid with three interchangeable bracket holders (distances 54 ± 0.5 mm, 59 ± 0.5 mm, 64 ± 0.5 mm). Connect the annular quartz tube (with cooling jacket) via a PTFE sleeve to the glass sleeve on the lid. Install the external borosilicate reservoir (0.6 L) to the reactor using the one‑way valve and connect all hoses (≈0.15 L total). Ensure the complete system volume is 3 L. Insert the four GL15‑threaded caps (DIN 168) into the lower and upper ports, seal optics with PTFE tape, and place a glass stopper in the riser pipe for inert‑gas flushing. Place the assembled reactor inside a safety cabinet.

steps.title: Configure in‑line monitoring system
steps.instruction: Through two threaded ports install a temperature sensor and a USB spectrometer; seal with PTFE tape. Place pH, temperature and dissolved‑oxygen probes in the external reservoir. Connect a peristaltic pump to draw a small sample stream through a flow‑through cuvette linked to the USB spectrophotometer. Set up a custom LabVIEW program to record lamp spectrum, temperature, pH, DO, flow rate and to save data as text/CSV.

steps.title: Synthesize TiO₂‑PES membrane
steps.instruction: Prepare a casting solution containing commercial P25 TiO₂ (15 wt %), cationic ionomer Fumion (4 wt %) and polyethersulfone (PES, 20 wt %) dissolved in N‑methyl‑pyrrolidone (NMP). Cast a flat‑sheet film of 250 µm thickness, then immerse it in a water precipitation bath to form a porous membrane. The resulting TiO₂‑PES membrane contains 16 wt % Ti (EDX) and exhibits a band gap of 3.12 eV.

steps.title: Measure UV‑Vis and reflectance spectra
steps.instruction: Record the UV‑Vis absorption spectrum of a 50 µM amoxicillin (AMX) solution and the reflectance spectrum of the fabricated TiO₂‑PES membrane as described in the supporting information. Note that AMX absorbs <300 nm and the membrane reflectance minimum is at 350 nm.

steps.title: Prepare UV cut‑off filter solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve potassium hydrogen phthalate (KHP) to 1.5 g L⁻¹, potassium nitrate (KNO₃) to 61 g L⁻¹ and 182 g L⁻¹, and potassium nitrite (KNO₂) to 75 g L⁻¹ in deionised water. These solutions act as selective cut‑off filters: KNO₂ transmits visible light only, KNO₃ transmits visible + UVA, KHP transmits visible + UVA + UVB, and no filter transmits the full lamp spectrum including UVC.

steps.title: Introduce filter solutions into cooling flow
steps.instruction: Circulate the chosen filter solution (e.g., 61 g L⁻¹ KNO₃) through the void region of the annular quartz tube using the cooling water bath. This modifies the lamp spectrum without contacting the reaction mixture.

steps.title: Prepare buffered reaction solution
steps.instruction: Fill the reaction chamber with 0.285 L ultrapure water, add phosphate buffer to obtain 5 mM concentration, and adjust the pH to 7.0 with diluted NaOH or H₃PO₄.

steps.title: Set flow and stirring conditions
steps.instruction: Set the pump to a flow rate of 1 L min⁻¹ (well below the maximum 10 L min⁻¹ capability) and start magnetic stirring at 2000 rpm to ensure uniform mixing.

steps.title: Preheat mercury lamp
steps.instruction: Switch on the 150‑W medium‑pressure Hg lamp and allow it to stabilize for 20 min. Expect an initial temperature rise of ≈5 °C in the reactor.

steps.title: Add amoxicillin stock to reactor
steps.instruction: Inject 100 mL of a 1.5 mM AMX stock solution (pH 7) into the external reservoir. This yields a final AMX concentration of 50 µM (18 mg L⁻¹) throughout the 3 L system.

steps.title: Ensure homogeneous mixing
steps.instruction: Allow the system to circulate for ~30 s to achieve uniform distribution of AMX.

steps.title: Run photolysis, adsorption, and photocatalysis tests

substeps.instruction: Photolysis: keep the reactor empty of membrane and run under (i) no filter, (ii) 61 g L⁻¹ KNO₃, and (iii) 182 g L⁻¹ KNO₃. Record degradation over time.
Adsorption: place three TiO₂‑PES membrane pieces (7.5 × 9.5 cm each, 3.6 mg TiO₂ cm⁻², total area 214 cm²) in the bracket holders, keep the lamp off (dark) for 600 min and monitor AMX concentration.
Photocatalysis: use the same three membranes, turn the lamp on, and run with the 61 g L⁻¹ KNO₃ cut‑off filter. This condition gave a half‑life of ≈125 min in the study.

steps.title: Collect and store samples over 10 h
steps.instruction: Use the automated fraction collector to withdraw aliquots at predefined intervals for a total experimental duration of 10 h. Store samples appropriately for LC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Analyze samples by LC‑ESI‑HRMS
steps.instruction: Quantify residual AMX in each sample using an Orbitrap LC‑ESI‑HRMS system. Calculate the degradation degree as C_t / C_0 and transform to ln(C_t/C_0) for kinetic analysis.

steps.title: Calculate degradation kinetics
steps.instruction: Fit the ln‑linearised data to obtain pseudo‑first‑order rate constants (k) and half‑lives (t₁/₂). Reported values include: k = 5.53 × 10⁻³ min⁻¹ (t₁/₂ ≈ 125 min, photocatalysis with 61 g L⁻¹ KNO₃), k = 0.041 min⁻¹ (t₁/₂ ≈ 16 min, photolysis without filter), k = 1.79 × 10⁻³ min⁻¹ (t₁/₂ ≈ 387 min, photolysis with 61 g L⁻¹ KNO₃), k = 9.18 × 10⁻⁴ min⁻¹ (t₁/₂ ≈ 755 min, photolysis with 182 g L⁻¹ KNO₃). Coefficients of determination (R²) range from 0.959 to 0.999.

steps.title: Test membrane reusability
steps.instruction: Repeat the photocatalytic degradation experiment with the same TiO₂‑PES membrane for multiple cycles to assess performance retention, as described in the supporting information (section S5).
